panels.visual: Aristotle (dandy, rings, neat beard, fine cloak) crouching in a sunny garden with a notebook, carefully watching two real cats washing and stalking
panels.caption: Aristotle watched real cats.

panels.visual: Plato gazing dreamily upward at a glowing, golden, perfect, ideal cat floating in the clouds, hands clasped, while Aristotle in the corner rolls his eyes
panels.caption: Plato dreamed of the perfect cat.

panels.visual: Aristotle counting a cat's whiskers and measuring its paw with a ruler, notes and sketches of birds, plants and a weathervane around him
panels.caption: Count, compare, take them apart.

panels.visual: Aristotle in the Lyceum surrounded by animals, plants, weather charts and scrolls on politics, an exuberant scholar, Glauka the owl on a shelf
panels.caption: He studied animals, plants, weather and politics.

panels.visual: Aristotle at a writing table with his young son Nicomachus (a small boy with curly hair) leaning on his arm, both reading a scroll
panels.caption: He wrote a book on how to live well, named after his son Nicomachus.

panels.visual: A big unrolled scroll with the title NICOMACHEAN ETHICS and the words HOW TO LIVE WELL, light shining from it
panels.caption: The Nicomachean Ethics.

panels.visual: A tree in full blossom with golden fruit and white flowers growing from a scroll, a big word EUDAIMONIA on a ribbon
panels.caption: The goal of life is eudaimonia: flourishing.

speech.speaker: Aristotle
speech.text: Flourish by being good at being human.

panels.visual: Medieval scholars in hooded robes bowing deeply before a tall stack of Aristotle's books on a desk, candlelit monastery library, centuries passing as a calendar
panels.caption: For over a thousand years people believed what he wrote.

panels.visual: Aristotle explaining with a lead ball and a wooden ball held up in each hand, a thought-bubble of the lead ball falling first; a tick next to it, it looks right
panels.caption: He wrote that heavy things fall faster than light ones. It sounds right.

panels.visual: A tall church tower in Delft in 1586 with Simon Stevin (Flemish engineer, ruff collar, beard) on the top holding two lead balls over the parapet, a friend waiting far below with a hand cupped to his ear
panels.caption: In 1586 Simon Stevin dropped two lead balls from a church tower in Delft.

panels.visual: Two lead balls, one big and one small, falling side by side from the tower with speed lines, the friend below with eyes shut listening, a single big sound-effect
panels.caption: They hit the ground together. A thousand years earlier John Philoponus had already doubted Aristotle.

panels.visual: A small old Italian scholar (Galileo, in a doctor's robe) on the Leaning Tower of Pisa dropping balls, dotted memory-frame, a question mark and a stamp
panels.caption: The Galileo and Pisa story may never have happened. Galileo did prove it with balls rolling down slopes.
